name: 魚地心 広島八丁堀店 (Uochishin Hiroshima Hatchobori)

claims.text: Sashimi, simmered, and grilled seafood dishes are served with standard Japanese soy sauce and ponzu, which contain wheat.

name: ビーガン フルーツカフェ タマル 紙屋町店 (Vegan Fruits Cafe Tamaru Kamiyacho)

claims.text: The entire menu is plant-based, made without eggs, dairy, or white sugar, so vegan diners do not need to scrutinize individual dishes.

name: 和食屋 きくお (Washokuya Kikuo)

claims.text: The signature simmered dishes are built on a soy-based broth, indicating standard (wheat-containing) soy sauce is central to the cooking.

name: わたしの食卓 紙屋町店 (Watashi no Shokutaku Kamiyacho-ten)

claims.text: Set meals such as miso-simmered mackerel and pork kimchi rely on regular soy sauce and miso, which contain wheat.
Okonomiyaki is wheat-batter based and cooked on a shared griddle alongside noodles and other floured items, so cross-contact with gluten is inherent to the cooking style.
Okonomi/teppan sauces and the izakaya's soy-seasoned dishes use standard wheat-containing soy sauce; no gluten-free sauce is documented.
Dishes share a single teppan griddle used for meat, egg and seafood, and okonomiyaki batter/dashi contain egg and bonito, so vegan separation is not feasible here.
Yakitori tare glaze is soy-sauce and mirin based, which contains wheat; the meal is also often finished with a wheat-noodle chicken ramen.

name: 焼がきのはやし (Yakigaki no Hayashi)

claims.text: Oyster dishes are seasoned in the traditional Japanese style (soy sauce, ponzu), which normally contains wheat; no gluten-free seasoning is documented.
The kitchen is an oyster specialty kitchen; effectively all dishes are oyster/seafood based, so there is no separation suitable for vegan diners.

The shop has reportedly conducted norovirus testing on its oysters for about ten years with zero detections, indicating attention to oyster food safety (note: this concerns shellfish safety, not allergen handling).

name: 焼鳥かけはし 銀山 (Yakitori Kakehashi Kanayama)

claims.text: As a yakitori and izakaya kitchen, grilled skewers, fried items, and the hotpot share seasonings and surfaces built on wheat-containing soy sauce and tare; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Tare and dipping/seasoning sauces for the grilled chicken are based on standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.
The kitchen is built entirely around chicken, with broths and seasonings of animal/soy origin, so plant-based dishes would share equipment and stocks with meat.
